bull_case_summary: Sandisk has $8.743bn adjusted annual FCF after major prepayment/investment deductions and actual debt reduction to zero. Round two defends cash-normalised resilience and customer-growth upside rather than treating a peak-sensitive 6.30x estimate as permanent value.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts adjusted cash and debt repayment but emphasises the more restrained 3.60% FCF yield. Two-thirds pricing contribution and 79.20% adjusted quarterly operating margin leave through-cycle returns sensitive despite debt-free survival capacity.
key_points_of_agreement: Adjusted cash strength and debt repayment are verified.
Pricing and exceptional margins cannot be capitalised permanently.
Customer deposits and commitments constrain freely available cash.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether normalised cash resilience provides sufficient compensation for NAND cycle sensitivity at current capitalisation.
unresolved_uncertainties: Through-cycle customer economics and sustainable pricing/margins.
Free cash availability after deposits/commitments and historical corporate-action comparability.
